edits.value_json: Early forms are described as small marks above and below a central stroke. The marks later lengthened and joined into a cross-like form; Chu examples show that joining had begun before small seal script. Forms are also recorded in bronze inscriptions, small seal script, and the Shuowen entry, but the evidence does not establish a complete graphic sequence. The selected oracle-bone-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. (ref013, ref016, ref024, ref026, ref028, ref029, ref030)

The Shuowen entry glosses 米 as grain seed and interprets its form as depicting grain from a plant. This is a lexicographic interpretation, not independent confirmation of the graph’s origin. (ref003, ref018)

米 is reported in oracle-bone use for rice or grain. Scholarly discussion identifies its early referent as probably dehusked grain broadly, rather than a single crop; the precise first-use date and inscription context are unresolved. (ref014, ref016, ref017, ref028, ref030)
米 commonly means rice in modern usage. (ref001, ref002, ref016, ref028, ref030)

Other reported early uses include writing 敉 ‘pacify’, a sacrificial name, and clan names. Their inscription contexts and relationship, if any, to the grain meaning are unresolved, so they are not treated as semantic developments or separate senses. (ref014, ref017, ref031)

米 pictures scattered grain. Its early referent was probably dehusked grain broadly; today it commonly means rice. In Japanese, 米 also writes “metre”: 米突 rendered French mètre by sound, and 米 later became a shorter spelling. (ref014, ref016, ref022, ref028, ref030)
